title: Proof Protocol
concept: For when ‘I promise’ isn’t enough any more: a specific change, evidence you can both see, and a set time window, so nobody has to take it on faith.
whenToUse: When one of you asks for a real change and all that comes back is “I promise”, with no plan behind it. Use it instead of waiting for things to get better.
steps: Name the change — pick something specific you can both see.
Decide what counts — agree what ‘met’, ‘partial’ and ‘missed’ will look like.
Set a time window — agree a start date, an end date and when you’ll check in.
Keep the record short — a count or a table is enough — and look at it together at the check-in, where feelings and questions come first.
Check in — decide together whether to keep going, change it, or call it done.
Missed twice and nobody’s said so? Raise it at the next check-in.

phrases.text: I need proof, not a promise. The change: ___. Evidence: ___. Window: ___. Check-in: ___.
I’m committing to ___, visible as ___, through ___.
At check-in: how are we each feeling? Then let’s look at the record together.

working: After rows, A has been going quiet with no return time. The change: every Pause + Return gets an exact return time. Each return is noted, kept or not; they look at it together at the 14-day check-in. A keeps all six. B says the evenings feel less tense.
notWorking: B promises, “I’ll be better at communicating.” Ten days later B goes quiet after a row again, and neither of them can say whether the promise was kept: no specific behaviour, nothing to check, no time window.
activity: Today, on a sticky note, write the change, what you’ll both see, the dates, and when you’ll look at it. Both initial it.
